html:
The Wangkatha, also written Wongatha or Wongi, are Aboriginal Australian peoples of the Eastern Goldfields of Western Australia. The name covers a language and the shared identity of several groups whose country includes the towns of Kalgoorlie, Coolgardie, Menzies, Leonora and Laverton. The map shows them as Wangkathaa from 1600 to 1815.

Their speech is part of the Western Desert language of the Western Desert cultural bloc. Neighbours included the Koara to the northwest, the Kalaamaya to the west and the Kalaako and Malpa to the south.

Gold was found at Coolgardie in 1892 and at Kalgoorlie in 1893, and the Goldfields rush brought tens of thousands of miners into this dry country within a few years. Water holes were taken and fouled, and Wangkatha people were pushed to the edges of the new towns.
